title: Configure device access control using local passwords

questions.question: Which command configure the enable password for a router or switch?

correct.explanation: enable secret stores the privileged EXEC password as a one-way hash — preferred over cleartext enable password.

incorrect.explanation: password enable is invalid syntax — privileged password uses enable secret or enable password.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#password enable Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#enable secret Password20! satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#password enable Password20! does not.

incorrect.explanation: enable Password20! misses the secret keyword — IOS expects enable secret for hashed storage.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#enable Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#enable secret Password20! satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#enable Password20! does not.

incorrect.explanation: secret enable reverses the keyword order — correct form is enable secret.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#secret enable Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#enable secret Password20! satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#secret enable Password20! does not.

answerReview.examTip: Privileged mode → enable secret (hashed). Line/login passwords are separate.

questions.question: You need to set the login password for Telnet. Which command you type first?

correct.explanation: Telnet/SSH login passwords are configured under line vty 0 15 (or 0 4 on older platforms) — start there before password/login.

incorrect.explanation: Interface VLAN 1 configures SVI IP — not VTY line passwords for remote Telnet access.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Configuring SVI when VTY lines are needed
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#interface vlan 1 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#interface vlan 1 does not.

incorrect.explanation: Console line secures local serial/console access — Telnet uses virtual terminal (VTY) lines.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using console line for Telnet password
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#line console 1 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#line console 1 does not.

incorrect.explanation: Auxiliary line is legacy dial/modem access — Telnet targets VTY lines, not aux.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting aux line for Telnet configuration
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#line aux 1 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#line aux 1 does not.

answerReview.examTip: Remote login (Telnet/SSH) → line vty first. Console → line console 0.

questions.question: You have set the enable password using enable password Password20!. However, when you try to get to a privileged exec prompt, the router states that you are using an incorrect password. What is the problem?
choices: You originally entered the wrong password.
The enable secret password is set to something else.
The password Password20! contains a special character.
The password is too long and has been truncated.

correct.explanation: enable secret overrides enable password — if secret is set to something else, the plain enable password is ignored.

incorrect.explanation: You may be typing the right enable password — but enable secret takes precedence when both exist.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Wrong password typed as root cause
incorrect.whatItDoes: You originally entered the wrong password. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", The enable secret password is set to something else. satisfies what this question tests — You originally entered the wrong password. does not.

incorrect.explanation: IOS accepts special characters in passwords — the conflict is enable secret overriding enable password.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The password Password20! contains a special character. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", The enable secret password is set to something else. satisfies what this question tests — The password Password20! contains a special character. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Password length limits exist but secret override is the typical cause of this symptom.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The password is too long and has been truncated. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", The enable secret password is set to something else. satisfies what this question tests — The password is too long and has been truncated. does not.

answerReview.examTip: Troubleshoot enable: show running-config | include enable — look for enable secret first.

questions.question: Which command(s) will set a password and require login for a line?

correct.explanation: password <pwd> then login under config-line — password alone does nothing until login is enabled.

incorrect.explanation: set password and request login are not valid IOS line commands.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config-line)#set password Password20! Router(config-line)#request login names a DHCP DORA message step that may not be the phase described in the stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config-line)#password Password20! Router(config-line)#login satisfies what this question tests — Router(config-line)#set password Password20! Router(config-line)#request login does not.

incorrect.explanation: login password is wrong syntax — sequence is password then login.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config-line)#password Password20! Router(config-line)#login password points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config-line)#password Password20! Router(config-line)#login satisfies what this question tests — Router(config-line)#password Password20! Router(config-line)#login password does not.

incorrect.explanation: login password <pwd> is invalid — set password, then login on separate lines.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config-line)#login password Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config-line)#password Password20! Router(config-line)#login satisfies what this question tests — Router(config-line)#login password Password20! does not.

answerReview.examTip: VTY password: line vty 0 4 → password <pwd> → login → transport input ssh.

questions.question: You Telnet to a switch and receive the error Password required, but none set.[Connection to 192.168.1.1 closed by foreign host]. What is the problem?
choices: The enable secret is not set.
The enable password is not set.
The line login password is not set.

correct.explanation: login is configured but no password (or local user) on the vty line — Telnet rejects with "Password required, but none set".

incorrect.explanation: Enable secret affects privileged mode (#) — this error is a line login password missing.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Enable secret for vty login error
incorrect.whatItDoes: The enable secret is not set. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", The line login password is not set. satisfies what this question tests — The enable secret is not set. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Enable password is for privileged EXEC — vty needs password/login or login local.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The enable password is not set. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", The line login password is not set. satisfies what this question tests — The enable password is not set. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Admin down gives a different error — "Password required, but none set" means login without a password.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The line is administratively down. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", The line login password is not set. satisfies what this question tests — The line is administratively down. does not.

answerReview.examTip: Telnet fail messages: no password set = add password + login or username + login local.

questions.question: Identify required before generating the encryption keys for SSH on a router or switch?
choices: Setting the hostname and domain name

correct.explanation: SSH key generation requires hostname and ip domain-name — IOS embeds them in the certificate distinguished name.

incorrect.explanation: Clock/NTP helps logs and certs elsewhere — hostname + domain-name are mandatory before crypto key generate rsa.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Setting the time and date points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Setting the hostname and domain name satisfies what this question tests — Setting the time and date does not.

incorrect.explanation: Key modulus is specified at generation time — not a separate prerequisite step.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Setting the key strength points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Setting the hostname and domain name satisfies what this question tests — Setting the key strength does not.

incorrect.explanation: No key repository config exists — set hostname and domain-name first.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Setting the key repository points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Setting the hostname and domain name satisfies what this question tests — Setting the key repository does not.

answerReview.examTip: SSH setup order: hostname → ip domain-name → crypto key generate rsa → ip ssh version 2.

questions.question: Which command enable SSH version 2 for logins?

correct.explanation: ip ssh version 2 in global config forces SSHv2 — v1 is disabled when v2 is enabled.

incorrect.explanation: version 2 under config-line is invalid — SSH version is a global setting.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config-line)#version 2 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#ip ssh version 2 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config-line)#version 2 does not.

incorrect.explanation: config-ssh mode does not exist — use Router(config)# ip ssh version 2.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config-ssh)#version 2 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#ip ssh version 2 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config-ssh)#version 2 does not.

incorrect.explanation: ssh version 2 omits ip keyword — correct command is ip ssh version 2.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#ssh version 2 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#ip ssh version 2 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#ssh version 2 does not.

answerReview.examTip: SSHv2: ip ssh version 2 + RSA modulus ≥ 768 (1024+ recommended) + transport input ssh on vty.

questions.question: Which command configure the router or switch to allow SSH as a protocol for management with a fallback of Telnet?

correct.explanation: transport input ssh telnet under line vty allows SSH first with Telnet fallback on those lines.

incorrect.explanation: login ssh telnet is not valid — transport protocols are set with transport input on the line.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#login ssh telnet uses cleartext Telnet for remote device management.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Device management (local device access): Switch(config-line)#transport ssh telnet protects credentials in transit — Switch(config)#login ssh telnet uses cleartext remote access.

incorrect.explanation: Close — but login sets auth, not transport — use transport input ssh telnet.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-line)#login ssh telnet uses cleartext Telnet for remote device management.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Device management (local device access): Switch(config-line)#transport ssh telnet protects credentials in transit — Switch(config-line)#login ssh telnet uses cleartext remote access.

incorrect.explanation: transport is a line command, not global config.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#transport ssh telnet uses cleartext Telnet for remote device management.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Device management (local device access): Switch(config-line)#transport ssh telnet protects credentials in transit — Switch(config)#transport ssh telnet uses cleartext remote access.

answerReview.examTip: VTY transport: transport input ssh (SSH only) | transport input ssh telnet (both) | transport input none (lock out).

questions.question: Why should Telnet be replaced with SSH?
choices: SSH makes it easier to create ACLs for access.

correct.explanation: Replace Telnet with SSH because SSH encrypts the entire session — credentials and commands are not sent in cleartext.

incorrect.explanation: Telnet has no encryption (not merely weak) — every byte is readable on the wire.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Telnet has weak encryption. uses cleartext Telnet for remote device management.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Device management (local device access): SSH is encrypted. protects credentials in transit — Telnet has weak encryption. uses cleartext remote access.

incorrect.explanation: File copy uses SCP/SFTP — not the primary reason to swap Telnet for SSH.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: SSH file copy as main benefit
incorrect.whatItDoes: SSH allows for file copy. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", SSH is encrypted. satisfies what this question tests — SSH allows for file copy. does not.

incorrect.explanation: ACLs control who connects — SSH adds encryption independent of ACL rules.
incorrect.whatItDoes: SSH makes it easier to create ACLs for access. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", SSH is encrypted. satisfies what this question tests — SSH makes it easier to create ACLs for access. does not.

answerReview.examTip: Telnet = TCP/23 cleartext | SSH = TCP/22 encrypted — disable Telnet: transport input ssh.

questions.question: Which command create and apply an access list to secure router or switch management?
choices: Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#interface vlan 1 Switch(config-if)#ip access-group 1 in
Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 Switch(config-line)#ip access-group 1 in
Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 Switch(config-line)#ip access-class 1 in
Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#ip access-group 1 in

correct.explanation: Apply ACL to vty lines with ip access-class <num> in — restricts who can Telnet/SSH to the device.

incorrect.explanation: ip access-group on SVI filters transit/routed traffic — not management sessions on vty.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#interface vlan 1 Switch(config-if)#ip access-group 1 in applies an ACL type (standard vs extended) or number range that may not match placement rules here.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: ACL placement/match (local device access): Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 Switch(config-line)#ip access-class 1 in uses the right ACL type and position — Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#interface vlan 1 Switch(config-if)#ip access-group 1 in mismatches standard vs extended rules.

incorrect.explanation: ip access-group is for interfaces — vty lines use ip access-class.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 Switch(config-line)#ip access-group 1 in applies an ACL type (standard vs extended) or number range that may not match placement rules here.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: ACL placement/match (local device access): Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 Switch(config-line)#ip access-class 1 in uses the right ACL type and position — Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 Switch(config-line)#ip access-group 1 in mismatches standard vs extended rules.

incorrect.explanation: ip access-group in global config is invalid — define ACL, then ip access-class under line vty.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#ip access-group 1 in applies an ACL type (standard vs extended) or number range that may not match placement rules here.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: ACL placement/match (local device access): Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#line vty 0 5 Switch(config-line)#ip access-class 1 in uses the right ACL type and position — Switch(config)#access-list 1 permit host 192.168.1.5 Switch(config)#ip access-group 1 in mismatches standard vs extended rules.

answerReview.examTip: Mgmt ACL: access-list 1 permit host <admin-ip> → line vty 0 15 → access-class 1 in.

questions.question: You have created the SSH encryption keys, but you cannot enable SSH version 2. What is the problem?
choices: The time and date need to be corrected.
The key strength needs to be 768 bits or higher.
The DNS server is not configured.
There is no host record for the switch or router.

correct.explanation: SSHv2 requires RSA keys of at least 768 bits — generate with crypto key generate rsa modulus 1024 (or higher).

incorrect.explanation: Clock sync helps logging — it does not block ip ssh version 2 like insufficient key modulus does.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The time and date need to be corrected. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", The key strength needs to be 768 bits or higher. satisfies what this question tests — The time and date need to be corrected. does not.

incorrect.explanation: DNS is not required for SSHv2 — key size is the usual blocker.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The DNS server is not configured. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", The key strength needs to be 768 bits or higher. satisfies what this question tests — The DNS server is not configured. does not.

incorrect.explanation: No DNS host record is needed on-device — RSA modulus ≥ 768 enables v2.
incorrect.whatItDoes: There is no host record for the switch or router. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", The key strength needs to be 768 bits or higher. satisfies what this question tests — There is no host record for the switch or router. does not.

answerReview.examTip: SSHv2 fail: regenerate keys — crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048 then ip ssh version 2.

questions.question: Which command configure a local user for SSH access?

correct.explanation: username <name> password <secret> in global config creates a local user for login local authentication.

incorrect.explanation: account submode is not valid IOS — use username in global config.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#account user1 Router(config-acct)#password Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#username user1 password Password20! satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#account user1 Router(config-acct)#password Password20! does not.

incorrect.explanation: user alone is incomplete — syntax is username <name> password|secret <pwd>.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#user user1 Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#username user1 password Password20! satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#user user1 Password20! does not.

incorrect.explanation: user-account is not Cisco syntax — use username.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#user-account user1 password Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#username user1 password Password20! satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#user-account user1 password Password20! does not.

answerReview.examTip: Prefer username bob secret <pwd> (hashed) over password (weak) + login local on vty.

questions.question: Which command generate the encryption keys for SSH?

correct.explanation: crypto key generate rsa in global config creates the RSA key pair SSH uses for encryption.

incorrect.explanation: Keyword order matters — crypto key generate rsa, not generate crypto key rsa.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#generate crypto key rsa points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#crypto key generate rsa satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#generate crypto key rsa does not.

incorrect.explanation: crypto generate key rsa scrambles middle keywords — use crypto key generate rsa.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#crypto generate key rsa points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#crypto key generate rsa satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#crypto generate key rsa does not.

incorrect.explanation: Key generation runs in config mode (Router(config)#), not privileged EXEC alone.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: RSA key in exec mode only
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#crypto key generate rsa points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Router(config)#crypto key generate rsa satisfies what this question tests — Router#crypto key generate rsa does not.

answerReview.examTip: Verify SSH: show ip ssh — keys present, version 2.0, timeout/authentication retries.

questions.question: Which command disable auto-disconnect for idle privileged exec sessions?

correct.explanation: exec-timeout 0 0 under config-line disables idle disconnect — 0 minutes, 0 seconds = never timeout.

incorrect.explanation: exec-timeout is a line command, not global config.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#exec-timeout 0 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config-line)#exec-timeout 0 0 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#exec-timeout 0 does not.

incorrect.explanation: timeout alone is invalid — IOS uses exec-timeout <min> <sec>.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-line)#timeout 0 0 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config-line)#exec-timeout 0 0 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-line)#timeout 0 0 does not.

incorrect.explanation: no exec-timeout restores default (10 min) — use exec-timeout 0 0 to disable.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-line)#no exec-timeout points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config-line)#exec-timeout 0 0 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-line)#no exec-timeout does not.

answerReview.examTip: Line timeout: exec-timeout 30 0 = 30 min idle | exec-timeout 0 0 = never disconnect.

questions.question:
Switch# show users
    Line       User       Host(s)              Idle       Location
*  0 con 0                idle                 0          local
   1 vty 0     admin      192.168.1.50         0          local
   2 vty 1                idle                 5          local

you have listed all management sessions on the switch. On which line are you connected?

correct.explanation: The asterisk (*) marks your current session — if you Telnet'd as admin from 192.168.1.50, you're on VTY 0.

incorrect.explanation: Console 0 is line 0 — when connected via vty, the * appears on your vty line, not console.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Console 0 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", VTY 0 satisfies what this question tests — Console 0 does not.

incorrect.explanation: VTY 1 shows idle 5 with no user — your active admin session is VTY 0.
incorrect.whatItDoes: VTY 1 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", VTY 0 satisfies what this question tests — VTY 1 does not.

incorrect.explanation: Only vty 0–1 exist in the output — VTY 2 is not listed.
incorrect.whatItDoes: VTY 2 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", VTY 0 satisfies what this question tests — VTY 2 does not.

answerReview.examTip: show users / show line: * = your session | clear line vty <n> kicks another admin.

questions.question: You want to turn on local authentication so that a user must supply a username and password when managing the switch. You have created the username and password combinations on the switch. Which command direct SSH and Telnet to use this authentication model?

correct.explanation: login local on line vty tells SSH/Telnet to authenticate against the local username database you created.

incorrect.explanation: aaa new-model enables full AAA — simple local auth only needs login local on the line.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: aaa new-model for basic local login
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#new aaa model points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config-line)#login local satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#new aaa model does not.

incorrect.explanation: local authentication is not a global command — use login local under line vty.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#local authentication points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config-line)#login local satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#local authentication does not.

incorrect.explanation: local authentication is invalid under config-line — the command is login local.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-line)#local authentication points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config-line)#login local satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-line)#local authentication does not.

answerReview.examTip: Local auth chain: username → line vty 0 15 → login local → transport input ssh.

questions.question: You need to change the default idle time before disconnection of privileged exec mode for network administrators. Which command change it to 30 minutes?

correct.explanation: exec-timeout 30 0 under config-line sets 30 minutes idle before disconnect (minutes, then seconds).

incorrect.explanation: exec-timeout belongs under line config, not global config.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#exec-timeout 30 0 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config-line)#exec-timeout 30 0 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#exec-timeout 30 0 does not.

incorrect.explanation: exec-timeout 0 30 means 0 minutes, 30 seconds — not 30 minutes.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-line)#exec-timeout 0 30 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config-line)#exec-timeout 30 0 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-line)#exec-timeout 0 30 does not.

incorrect.explanation: timeout without exec- is invalid IOS syntax.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-line)#timeout 30 0 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch(config-line)#exec-timeout 30 0 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-line)#timeout 30 0 does not.

answerReview.examTip: exec-timeout <minutes> <seconds> on line con 0 and line vty — default is often 10 0.

questions.question: You need to disconnect a network admin from the switch or router. Which command would you use?

correct.explanation: clear line vty 2 from privileged EXEC terminates the session on vty 2 — kicks that admin off.

incorrect.explanation: no enable secret removes your enable password — it does not disconnect a remote vty user.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#no enable secret points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for local device access.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "local device access", Switch#clear line vty 2 satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#no enable secret does not.
